{statusCards.map((card, idx) => ( ))} {/* Runway calculation */}

The "Runway" Calculation

Core formula:

Runway (days) = Effective Stock ÷ Effective Daily Velocity
{/* Velocity resolution */}

Effective Daily Velocity — Resolution Priority

  1. 1. ERP dailyAverageSales field — if your Inventory Report includes this column, it is used unconditionally and overrides all calculations. This ensures runway stays consistent with your ERP system.
  2. 2. Weighted calculation from imported sales — if no ERP value exists, the system calculates a weighted average from transaction history over the selected lookback window.
  3. 3. Stored averageDailySales — last resort fallback from the product record if no other source is available.
{/* Include Incoming toggle */}

Strategy Engine: "Include Incoming" Toggle

In the Strategy Engine toolbar, toggle Incoming Included to add in-transit stock to your effective stock figure for more aggressive runway planning.

Standard (Conservative) Effective Stock = On Hand
Incoming Included Effective Stock = On Hand + Incoming
{/* Returns */}

Returns & Quality Control

Refunds are imported via the Refund Report upload. Data is aggregated by SKU and matched against the selected date period.

Return Rate Formula

(Returned Units ÷ Sold Units) × 100

Calculated within the same period. Used to flag quality and listing issues.

High Return Alert

Return rate exceeding 5% (default, configurable in Configuration → Alert Settings) triggers a warning badge. Common causes: misleading listing description, packaging or QC issues.

{/* Velocity Settings */}

Velocity Lookback Settings

Average Daily Sales is calculated from imported transaction history over the selected lookback window. Change the default in{' '} Configuration → System Behaviour. A per-session override is also available in the Strategy Engine toolbar.

ERP Override

If your Inventory Report includes a dailyAverageSales column, that value overrides the lookback calculation entirely for that SKU.

{/* Data Hierarchy */}

Data Hierarchy & "Ghost" Products

Master SKU vs. Aliases

The system revolves around the Master SKU from your Inventory Report. Platform listings are linked via Aliases. Sales from all aliases aggregate into the Master SKU's velocity and P&L.

Inactive / "Ghost" Products

Products with 0 Stock AND 0 Sales in the selected period are hidden by default. Toggle the eye icon in the filter bar to reveal them.

)} {/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════ TAB 2 — FINANCIAL FORMULAS ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════ */} {activeTab === 'financial' && (
{/* Tax Basis */}

Tax Basis

All monetary values are shown inc. VAT by default across the app. Metrics explicitly labelled "ex tax" are the exception — mainly in the Cost Management view when analysing COGS and fee structures.

{/* Core P&L Formulas */}

Core P&L Formulas

Net Profit (per unit)

(Selling Price + Extra Freight) − (COGS + Platform Fee + Ad Spend + Postage + WMS + Other Fees)

Net Margin %

(Net Profit ÷ Selling Price) × 100

Return-Adjusted Revenue

Gross Revenue − (Refund Amount + Resend Cost)

Return = Refund Amount + Resend Cost. Both are deducted from gross revenue. Sourced from the Refund Report or embedded resend_amt/refund_amt columns in the Sales Report.

TACoS (Total Advertising Cost of Sales)

(Total Ad Spend ÷ Total Revenue) × 100

Primary measure of advertising efficiency. Ad costs are imported via the Sales Transaction Report.

 {/* Optimal Price Formulas */}

Optimal Price Engine Formulas

The Optimal Price Engine is separate from the Strategy Engine. It runs automatically on sales import and cohort rebuild, and surfaces profit-maximising price suggestions as confidence badges and tooltips in the Strategy table. The formulas below define how it works internally.

Daily Profit (per price point)

Daily Profit = (CA Price − Total Costs) × Median Daily Velocity

The price point with the highest Daily Profit is selected as the SKU-level optimal. Velocity is median weekly units ÷ 7 (not mean — suppresses spike weeks).

Confidence Score

Base = min(1.0, eligible transactions ÷ 30)

Capped at 0.3 if only 1 distinct price point observed. Boosted ×1.2 (max 1.0) if 3+ distinct price points observed.

Blended Price

Blended = (confidence × skuOptimal) + ((1 − confidence) × cohortOptimal)

At ≥90% confidence: pure SKU data. At <30%: pure cohort benchmark. Between 30–90%: proportional blend.

Final Recommended Price

snapTo99(applyGuardrails(blendedPrice))

Guardrails applied first (see below), then snapped to nearest £X.99. e.g. £108.34 → £107.99

{/* Guardrail Formulas */}

Strategy Guardrail Formulas

Applied in order after blending. The first constraint that fires wins.

1. Absolute Cost Floor

Min Price = Total Costs × 1.05

Hard stop. The engine will never recommend a selling price that results in a loss. Always enforced regardless of other settings.

2. Category Minimum Margin Floor

Min Price = Total Costs ÷ (1 − categoryMinMargin%)

Set per platform/category in Configuration → Platform Rules. Prevents recommendations that would breach your target margin threshold.

3. Maximum Price Ceiling

Max Price = CA Reference Price × 1.5

Prevents runaway increases. The recommended price can never exceed 150% of the current CA reference price.

 {/* Weighted Averages */}

Weighted Average Logic

All price and fee averages use a volume-weighted mean — not a simple average. This prevents a few high-volume, low-price orders from skewing results.

Weighted Avg Price

Sum(Order Revenue) ÷ Total Units Sold

Weighted Avg Fee

Sum(Fee Costs) ÷ Total Units Sold
{/* Trend Analysis */}

Trend Analysis (Period-over-Period)

All trend indicators use PoP logic — the current selected window compared against the immediately preceding window of identical length.

Last 7 Days

Compares [Today−7 → Yesterday] vs [Today−14 → Today−8]

Last 30 Days

Compares last 30 days vs the 30 days immediately prior

 {/* Cohort Benchmark */}

Cohort Benchmark (Layer 2)

When a SKU has fewer than 30 eligible transactions, the algorithm blends in a cohort benchmark from similar products. Here's how cohorts are built:

Log-Scale Price Buckets

Within each category, SKUs are grouped into price buckets using a log scale (so the £5–15 range and the £100–150 range each get a bucket, rather than cheap products dominating). Buckets with fewer than 3 SKUs are merged into their nearest neighbour.

Cohort Stats per Bucket

For each bucket: median velocity, median margin %, and price elasticity are computed. The cohort optimal price is the point on the elasticity curve that maximises estimated daily profit for the bucket midpoint.

Benchmark Refresh

Cohort benchmarks are rebuilt when new SKUs are added or when a SKU's CA price shifts it into a different price bucket. The app will prompt you when a rebuild is recommended after an import.

Ecosystem & Philosophy', desc: 'The core principles of Sello UK Hub.', icon: Globe, color: 'indigo', content: (

Browser-Native Design

Sello runs entirely in your browser. All data is stored locally — nothing is sent to any server unless you explicitly sync. This means it works offline, is fast, and your sensitive business data stays private.

Inventory First

The system anchors everything to a Master SKU from your ERP Inventory Report. Without a verified inventory layer, sales data is just noise. Always upload your Inventory Report before uploading sales.

What It Does

Sello is a business intelligence and pricing engine. It aggregates sales across platforms, tracks inventory health, calculates real margin, and surfaces data-backed price recommendations — all without manual spreadsheet work.

What It Does Not Do

It does not push price changes to platforms automatically. All recommendations are advisory — you review, approve, and apply them yourself. It does not manage listings, orders, or fulfilment.

Master SKU

Defined by your ERP Inventory Report. The single source of truth for a physical product — its name, category, brand, COGS, lead time, and warehouse stock level.

Platform Aliases

Amazon, eBay, and Etsy each assign their own SKU codes to your listings. Aliases tell the system: "this Amazon SKU AMZ-SP1057 is the same physical product as Master SKU SP1057-UK."

Aggregation

All sales for every alias are summed into the Master SKU. One product gets one velocity, one P&L, one recommendation — regardless of how many platforms it sells on.

Grade Levels (G1–G5)

Products can have a Grade Level (G1–G5) imported from the ERP report. G1/G2 are high performers; G4/G5 flag underperformers. Grades are displayed as colour-coded badges across Product Management and Strategy tables.

Inventory Status Tags

Products can carry status tags from the ERP: New Product, Clearance, etc. These influence Strategy Engine behaviour — e.g. New Products are excluded from decrease recommendations by default (configurable via the Fresh Stock Guard setting).

{/* Two systems callout */}

⚠ These are two separate systems

Strategy Engine

Stock-health rules engine. Looks at runway vs configurable thresholds and recommends INCREASE, DECREASE, or MAINTAIN with a fixed adjustment amount. Lives in the Strategy page table.

Optimal Price Engine

3-layer profit-maximisation algorithm. Analyses price-velocity history to find the price that maximises daily profit. Runs automatically on sales import. Results appear as confidence badges and tooltips on the Strategy table — they do not drive the INCREASE/DECREASE action.

{/* Strategy Engine */}

Strategy Engine — How It Works

The Strategy Engine evaluates each SKU's runway and applies configured rules to decide whether to increase, decrease, or maintain the current CA price:

INCREASE Runway < minimum runway weeks AND last 7-day qty > minimum velocity threshold
DECREASE Runway > high stock weeks, OR runway > medium stock weeks AND margin > minimum margin %
MAINTAIN Neither condition met, or product is in Fresh Stock Guard period, or off-season seasonal item

The adjusted price is calculated as:

New Price = Current CA Price ± max(price × adjustment%, fixed £ adjustment)

All thresholds (runway weeks, velocity minimum, adjustment %) are configurable in Configuration → Strategy Rules. Recommendations are generated on demand — trigger via the Recalculate button or by changing the velocity lookback.

{/* Optimal Price Engine */}

Optimal Price Engine — How It Works

Runs automatically when sales are imported or when a cohort rebuild is triggered. Results are displayed as a confidence badge on each row and as the "Optimal" column in the family group tooltip. The engine uses three layers:

Layer 1 — SKU Evidence

Builds a price-velocity curve from the SKU's own history, segmented into Price Eras defined by CA price change events. Within each era, velocity = median weekly units ÷ 7. Selects the price point with the highest Daily Profit = Margin × Velocity.

Layer 2 — Cohort Benchmark

When a SKU has fewer than 30 eligible transactions, the engine blends in a cohort benchmark from similar SKUs in the same category and log-scale price bucket. The confidence score (0–100%) determines how much weight SKU data vs cohort data gets in the final price.

Layer 3 — Guardrails

Three hard constraints applied in order: (1) Cost × 1.05 absolute floor, (2) category margin floor, (3) CA Price × 1.5 ceiling. Final price snaps to £X.99 psychological pricing.

Promotions as Elasticity Signals: Promotional transactions are not excluded — they are tagged as source: 'promo' and modelled as separate price points. This lets the engine learn from promo-period velocity without distorting organic recommendations.

How It Works

Type a plain-language question into the Global Search bar at the top. The AI parser converts your query into structured filters and returns matching SKUs. No need to manually set dropdowns or filter columns.

"Healthy SKUs with margin > 40% on Amazon"
"Critical stock under £10 in Home Category"
"Top 20% products by units sold last week"
"Overstock items with return rate above 5%"

Prefix with sku: to jump directly to a specific product deep dive. e.g. sku: SP1057-UK

Price Elasticity Insights

Open any SKU Deep Dive and select the Elasticity tab to see a scatter chart of observed price points vs daily velocity. The engine highlights the Profit Sweet Spot — the price where margin × velocity is maximised. The chart also shows confidence level and which data points came from organic vs promotional periods.

) }, { id: 'ops', title: '7. Operations, Promotions & Toolbox', desc: 'Day-to-day operational tools.', icon: Tag, color: 'pink', content: (

Promotion Planner

Create promotion events per platform and SKU group. Each event has a date range, discount type (% off), and scope (specific SKUs or whole shop).

  • • Active promotions appear as a [PROMO] tag in the Strategy table
  • • Completed promotions feed back into the pricing algorithm as elasticity signals
  • • Post-event velocity uplift vs BAU is visible in the Promotions page

Toolbox

  • Inventory Sync — generates platform-ready stock update files (CSV/XLSX) from your current stock levels, formatted for Amazon, eBay, etc.
  • Alias Generator — bulk-maps platform SKU codes to Master SKU IDs. Paste a platform export and it auto-suggests matches.
  • ERP Cross-Check — compares your ERP stock figures against the system's records to surface any discrepancies before they cause runway miscalculations.

Custom Reports

Build ad-hoc pivot reports using drag-and-drop dimensions (SKU, Category, Brand, Platform) and metrics (Revenue, Profit, Margin %, Units, Refund Rate, Ad Spend, TACoS, ASP, Stock, Days Cover). Set date ranges, apply filters, and export to XLSX. Layouts can be saved and re-run on fresh data.

) }, { id: 'maint', title: '8. Maintenance & Personalisation', desc: 'Keeping your Hub healthy and configured correctly.', icon: ShieldAlert, color: 'gray', content: (

Backup & Restore

All data is stored in browser local storage. Clearing your browser cache will wipe it permanently. Back up daily using the Backup Database button — it exports a .json file. Store it in SharePoint or OneDrive. Use Restore Database to reload from any prior backup.

⚠ If you switch browsers or devices, you must restore from a backup — data does not sync between browsers automatically.

Personalisation

Open User Profile (top-right avatar) to adjust the visual environment:

  • Theme colour — accent colour across all UI elements
  • Background image — custom wallpaper behind glass panels
  • Glass mode — light or dark glass surface
  • Glass opacity & blur — panel transparency and frosted depth
  • Ambient glass — subtle colour tint that picks up the background

Configuration Reference

Platform Rules

Set per-platform selling fee %, minimum margin %, and whether a platform is excluded from pricing calculations (e.g. wholesale channels).

System Behaviour

Set the default velocity lookback window (7 / 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 / All Time) and trigger a full product recalculation.

Alert Settings

Customise diagnostic thresholds: return rate alert %, margin below target %, velocity crash %, overstock days, dead stock minimum value.

Strategy Rules

Set increase/decrease thresholds: minimum runway weeks to trigger an increase, overstock weeks to trigger a decrease, safety margin floor, fresh stock guard days.

{/* Velocity Engine Section */}

Velocity Settings & Sensitivity

The "Average Daily Sales" metric is the heartbeat of the system. It is calculated based on the sales history you import, within the selected date range (e.g., Last 30 Days).

ERP Override Logic

Important: If your ERP Inventory Report provides a dailyAverageSales value for a product, that value will override any calculation from your imported sales report. This ensures inventory runway calculations are always consistent with your primary management system.

You can change the default calculation lookback period in Settings.

7 Days Lookback Highly reactive. Use this during peak seasons (e.g., Q4) to catch sudden spikes immediately.
30 Days Lookback Standard mode. Smooths out weekend dips and short-term anomalies.
90 Days Lookback Conservative. Best for restocking decisions on stable, long-tail products.
{/* Data Hierarchy Section - Moved from Manual to Operational as per original structure */}

Data Hierarchy & "Ghost" Products

Master SKU vs. Aliases

The system revolves around the Master SKU (from your Inventory Report). Platform listings (e.g., Amazon FBA, eBay) are linked via Aliases. Sales from all aliases are aggregated into the Master SKU's velocity.

Inactive / "Ghost" Products

To keep the dashboard clean, products with 0 Stock AND 0 Sales (in the selected period) are hidden by default. Toggle the "Show Inactive" eye icon in filters to reveal them.

)} {activeTab === 'financial' && (

Tax Basis (inc/ex)

Default is inc tax across the app. Only metrics explicitly labeled ‘ex tax’ are tax-excluded (mainly in the Cost Management view).

Weekly Reporting Cycles

The system automatically detects the latest date in your uploaded sales report and establishes a Friday-to-Thursday reporting cycle.

Fri 28 Nov - Thu 04 Dec

This full calendar history feeds the "Optimal Price" algorithm, allowing it to see trends over months rather than just weeks.

Trend Analysis (PoP)

All trend indicators (Volume Change, Revenue Change, Margin Trends) use PoP (Period-over-Period) logic.

Comparison Logic

"Current Selected Period vs Immediately Preceding Period of Same Length"

Example: Last 7 Days

Compares sales from [Today-7 to Yesterday] against [Today-14 to Today-8].

Example: Last 30 Days

Compares last 30 days against the 30 days prior to that window.

Ad Spend & TACoS Logic

TACoS Formula (Total Advertising Cost of Sales)

(Total Ad Spend / Total Revenue) × 100

This represents the percentage of total sales revenue consumed by advertising costs. It is the primary measure of advertising campaign efficiency.

Weighted Average Logic

When processing transaction reports, the system always uses a Volume-Weighted Average rather than a simple average.

Price Formula

(Sum of Revenue across all orders) / (Total Units Sold)

Fee Formula

(Sum of Fee Costs) / (Total Units Sold)

Margin Calculation

Net Profit Formula

(Selling Price + Extra Freight Income) - (COGS + Platform Comm. + Ad Spend + Postage + WMS + Other Fees)

Margin % Formula

(Net Profit / Selling Price) × 100

Net Revenue (Refund Adjusted)

Gross Sales Revenue - Total Refunded Value

* Refunds are imported separately and deducted from Gross Revenue when analyzing performance over time.

)} {activeTab === 'manual' && (
{manualSections.map(section => (

{section.desc}

))}

import { neon } from '@netlify/neon';

export default async (req: Request) => {
    try {
        const sql = neon(process.env.NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL!);

        await sql`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_snapshot (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                data TEXT,
                updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
                updated_by TEXT
            )
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transaction_history (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                sku TEXT NOT NULL,
                date TEXT NOT NULL,
                price NUMERIC,
                velocity NUMERIC,
                margin NUMERIC,
                profit NUMERIC,
                ads_spend NUMERIC,
                raw_ads_spend NUMERIC,
                platform TEXT,
                order_id TEXT,
                postcode TEXT,
                logistic_partner TEXT,
                logistic_service TEXT,
                real_postage NUMERIC,
                real_extra_freight NUMERIC,
                dedup_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
            )
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_sku 
            ON transaction_history(sku)
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_date 
            ON transaction_history(date)
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_metadata (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                last_push_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
                push_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0
            )
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_snapshot_uploads (
                upload_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                total_chunks INTEGER NOT NULL,
                created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
                updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
            )
        `;

        await sql`
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_snapshot_chunks (
                upload_id TEXT NOT NULL,
